title: Not just a room! Exploring the role of green innovations in the hospitality industry
summary: Purpose The manuscript investigates how green innovation practices (GIP) in hotels shape visitors' willingness to pay a premium for green accommodation through the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) lens. Design/methodology/approach This research paper used SMART PLS to analyse the data. This statistical tool is primarily used for predictive modelling, which emphasises the complex relationships among variables. Findings The results indicate that GIP not only indirectly contributes to the premium acceptance with multifaceted value perceptions and the functional, emotional and epistemic dimensions but also directly, which allows the tourism operators to achieve a 10–15% tariff premium by signalling credible sustainability promises. Research limitations/implications This study presents strong evidence on sustainable tourism dynamics; however, methodological decisions such as cross-sectional survey data and a convenience sample of 350 mainly urban Indian tourists limit causal conclusions and generalisation across demographics. Practical implications Policymakers can encourage this by providing incentives, such as tax rebates, to GIP adopters, in line with the National Tourism Policy, which aims to drive concerted industry-wide scaling of sustainable practices. Nonetheless, we must be very careful about excessive innovation; unless we align with local conditions, GIP will yield decreasing returns when viewed as elitist. In the long run, this SOR-based strategy will enable managers to consider sustainability as an active stimulus-response dynamic rather than a fixed requirement, and to develop profitable, resilient patterns in a climate-accountable era. Social implications The results of this study are a valuable addition to the body of knowledge about the complexity of sustainable tourism, specifically in the context of the Indian market, which is why the findings of this study can be viewed as an effective extension of the SOR framework, as it can help to understand how external stimuli can influence the internal assessment and behavioral patterns in the markets that are concerned about the environment. Originality/value This integrated framework clarifies how and for whom green innovation can translate into price-premium potential in the hotel sector and offers actionable guidance for managers to prioritise credible green practices and targeted communication to environmentally concerned segments to unlock sustainable revenue growth.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on the Saudi Higher Education Administration
summary: This study examines how the Saudi higher education administration is affected by the digital transformation, with a particular emphasis on student services management, data management, communication, administrative effectiveness, and decision-making. A representative sample of 930 administrative staff and information technology (IT) personnel from (6) public and private universities including; (Hail, Majmaah, Prince Satam bin Abdel- Aziz, Prince Sultan, Prince Meqren, and El-Faisal) universities, were given structured surveys as part of the research's quantitative, cross-sectional design, which was informed by the Technology-Organization-Environment paradigm. The results showed that digital transformation greatly improves decision-making and administrative efficiency, especially for administrative staff and in public universities. There are significant distinctions in staff positions and institutional types, meanwhile, with leadership seeing larger transformation advantages and public institutions benefiting more from government-backed efforts than IT professionals. Resistance to change, cybersecurity concerns, and a lack of technical skills are some of the main obstacles that have been found; these difficulties differ depending on the type of institution and personnel role. Improvements in data management, communication approaches, and student services were consistently indicated by respondents working across university departments and university contexts. The findings of the study indicated that although digitization has encouraged significant organizational improvements within Saudi higher education, it is necessary for organizational leaders and policymakers to encourage greater internal cohesion and growth opportunities to build more sustainable, competitive institutions in line with the goals of Vision 2030.

title: ESG Disclosure and Investment Decisions: Evidence from Jakarta Islamic Index
summary: Main Purpose - This study aims to analyze the impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure on investment decisions, focusing on companies listed in the Jakarta Islamic Index (JII). Method - This study uses secondary data obtained from annual reports and corporate sustainability reports for 2019-2024. The population was 60 companies registered in JII and 12 companies met the sample criteria. Data analysis was conducted using the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) based on the results of the Chow and Hausman tests. Main Findings - The results show that ESG disclosure and Cash to Total Assets have a positive effect on corporate investment decisions, while Return on Assets (ROA), Debt to Equity Ratio (DER), and Sales Growth have no effect on investment decisions. Theory and Practical Implications - These findings support Stakeholder Theory and Sharia Enterprise Theory, which emphasize the importance of social responsibility, ethics, and sustainability in creating long-term value for all stakeholders. These findings indicate that sharia investors in the Indonesian capital market consider sustainability aspects and compliance with sharia principles in making investment decisions. Novelty - Implementing ESG principles not only enhances a company's reputation but also reflects the values of maslahah (benefit), amanah (trustworthiness), and berkah (investment blessing) accordance with Islamic values. This will enhance company performance.

title: Artificial Intelligence And Fintech Startup Finance: Rebuilding Investment, Lending, And Financial Innovation
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a technology that is revolutionizing the financial services industry, empowering innovation, automation, and decision-making based on data. AI's influence on Financial Technology (FinTech) startups has revolutionized investment management, digital lending, and financial innovation, making startup finance more efficient, accessible, and competitive. In this paper, we explore the potential of AI to revolutionize investment, lending and financial decision-making processes in FinTech startups and analyse the opportunities and challenges of AI adoption. The study further explores the impact of AI-driven financial innovations on the growth, sustainability, and competitiveness of FinTech startups in the digital economy. This research is descriptive and exploratory, using secondary data from credible sources such as peer-reviewed journals, books, government publications, industry reports and other credible sources. The results highlight the positive impact of AI technologies, such as machine learning, predictive analytics, natural language processing, and generative AI, on operational efficiency, risk management, customer experience, and financial inclusion. However, issues like data privacy, cyber security, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations must be addressed through governance and policy support. Overall, the study highlights the importance of responsible AI adoption in driving sustainable growth, innovation, and long-term competitiveness in the evolving FinTech ecosystem.

title: Cybersecurity in digital transformation in healthcare: a systematic literature review
summary: The healthcare sector is going through a massive digital transformation that includes many technologies that facilitate the lives of patients and workers in the sector. Therefore, cybersecurity enhancements in this sector are an urgent necessity to protect sensitive data and ensure the continuity of safe healthcare services. This article conducted a systematic literature review (SLR) to identify the factors affecting cybersecurity in digital transformation, the methods used to protect systems, and the gaps in cybersecurity research within the healthcare sector. The review analyzed high-quality studies in the literature published in reputable journals to ensure the credibility of the findings. The results analysis of 90 studies showed that privacy concerns, trust, awareness, and training were the most common influencing factors. This study is among the first to explore the types of relationships between factors influencing cybersecurity in digital transformation, focusing on direct and indirect impact. Furthermore, the study included a discussion of the role of digital technologies in healthcare and the challenges they face, as well as a focus on the methods researchers have developed to address privacy and security issues.

title: FinTech investment and bank performance in the Eurozone: The moderating roles of regulatory quality and PSD2
summary: This paper aims to examine the impact of FinTech investment on bank performance in the Eurozone with emphasis on the moderating roles of regulatory quality and the Revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2). Applying a two-step robust Generalized Method of Moments estimator to a panel dataset of Eurozone banks between 2015–2023, using country-level FinTech venture capital investment as a proxy for FinTech intensity, we find that greater FinTech spending compresses net interest margins while significantly boosting asset efficiency (ROA) and has no immediate effect on equity returns or asset yields. Regulatory quality plays a decisive role: high regulatory quality both mitigate margin pressures and amplify efficiency gains from digital finance investments. In addition, PSD2 is seen to negatively affect ROA and YEA, as a reflection of short-term profitability pressures from increased compliance costs and competition. Moreover, a significant interaction effect of FinTech investment and PSD2 is observed which implies that the open-banking regime helped alleviate some of the margin pressures traditionally associated with FinTech expenditures. This study fills a gap in literature by empirically assessing how fintech investment and the regulatory environment influence performance outcomes. The results highlight the significance of focused investment strategies and regulatory balance in managing digital transformation in the banking industry, providing insightful information for regulators, policymakers, and financial institutions.

title: Energy transition and economic growth in low-income countries: the role of climate finance
summary: Abstract Although prices for renewable energy technologies have recently declined, many low-income countries still face barriers to deployment. The energy supply for their growing economies largely originates from the burning of fossil fuels. To avoid accelerating global greenhouse gas emissions, it is crucial that low-income countries enter a low-carbon growth path through the large-scale deployment of renewable energy. This is particularly relevant in countries that import fossil energy resources from global markets, where renewable energy deployment could be a tool for achieving independence and economic development. It can be beneficial in the short-run, for low-income countries with limited access to finance to rely on existing energy infrastructure. However, investment in renewable energy provides a long-run solution to preventing carbon lock-in by expanding existing infrastructure, such as pipelines or refineries. Therefore, we develop a theoretical model for long-run economic growth in import-dependent low-income countries. To produce renewable energy, a country must either attract international climate finance funds or substitute for other investments in the domestic economy to build a renewable energy capital stock. The results imply that sufficient and stable access to climate finance funds to transition to renewable energy accelerates long-run economic growth and welfare. Conversely, when investments in the energy transition crowds-out investment from other productive sectors in the economy, financing the energy transition can lead to income losses between 15 and 20% in the short- to medium-run. However, the energy transition does stimulate economic growth and welfare with an optimal allocation of capital in the long run. Furthermore, insufficient access to climate finance leads to rebound effects, accelerating demand for fossil energy and carbon emissions.

title: Policy-Driven Workforce Development and Integrated Skills as Predictors of Workforce Readiness in Thailand’s Digital Economy
summary: Aim/Purpose: This study aimed to examine how perceived policy‑driven workforce development initiatives enacted under the Thailand 4.0 national framework influence university students’ employability‑related skill development and their subsequent readiness to enter the labor market. Specifically, the research investigated the extent to which Policy and Workforce Development Initiatives (PWDI) contribute to students’ English Proficiency (EP), Digital and Technical Skills (DTS), and Soft Skills and Higher‑Order Thinking Skills (SHS), along with how these three skill domains shape overall Labor‑Market Readiness (LMR). Grounded in human capital and employability theories, workforce readiness is conceptualized as the result of integrated skills. By developing and validating a structural model grounded in current regional skill demands, this study provided empirical evidence on how policy initiatives translate into integrated skill outcomes among undergraduate learners. Introduction/Background: Across Southeast Asia, economies are undergoing rapid transformation driven by Industry 4.0 and 5.0 technologies, automation, and global connectivity. Thailand’s response to these shifts is captured in the Thailand 4.0 strategy, which emphasizes human capital development, digital transformation, and innovation capacity. Despite these policy efforts, labor‑market reports consistently highlight persistent skills gaps, particularly in English communication, digital literacy, and higher‑order cognitive abilities. Employers increasingly seek graduates who can operate in multilingual, technology‑mediated environments and who possess the adaptability, communication competence, and problem‑solving abilities required for dynamic workplaces. However, universities face ongoing challenges in aligning their curricula with rapidly changing workforce needs. Within this context, understanding the mechanisms through which policy initiatives influence skill development is essential. This research contributes to that understanding by modeling the direct pathways through which PWDI affect three core skill domains and, in turn, labor‑market readiness among undergraduate students. Methodology: A quantitative, cross‑sectional design was employed using data from 390 undergraduate students enrolled in seven academic programs at Bangkok University, Thailand. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire distributed via QR codes during class sessions. Each construct—PWDI, EP, DTS, SHS, and LMR—was measured using four validated items rated on a five‑point Likert scale. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) were conducted to evaluate the measurement and structural models. The CFA indicated excellent fit across all indicators (CMIN/DF = 1.283, GFI = .950, RMSEA = .027, CFI = .996), demonstrating strong construct validity. The structural model also exhibited robust fit (CMIN/DF = 1.280, GFI = .949, RMSEA = .027, CFI = .996). All six hypothesized paths were tested using standardized regression weights, critical ratios, and significance levels. Findings: The findings confirmed that PWDI significantly and positively influenced each of the three skill domains. The strongest effect was observed on Digital and Technical Skills (ß = .696), followed by Soft Skills and Higher‑Order Thinking Skills (ß = .680), and English Proficiency (ß = .656). These results highlighted the importance of policy mechanisms, such as work‑integrated learning, micro‑credentials, curriculum modernization, and teacher upskilling, in shaping student competencies across multiple domains. In turn, each skill domain demonstrated a significant positive effect on Labor‑Market Readiness. While all three skills contributed meaningfully, SHS displayed the strongest influence on LMR (ß = .369), followed by EP (ß = .333) and DTS (ß = .299). This suggests that soft skills and higher-order thinking skills help translate competencies into perceived workforce readiness. The model showed substantial explanatory power, with PWDI explaining 43.1% of the variance in EP, 48.4% in DTS, and 46.3% in SHS. Overall, the findings indicated that policy initiatives improve workplace-relevant skills, which in turn enhance students’ perceived readiness for the labor market. Contribution/Impact on Society: This study advances regional understanding of how educational policy, institutional initiatives, and curriculum reforms shape graduate employability in the context of digital transformation. The findings provide evidence that policy efforts under Thailand 4.0 can substantially enhance students’ skill development when effectively implemented at the university level. From a societal perspective, the findings reinforce the need for coordinated systems that align education with dynamic labor‑market needs. The study also highlights the importance of integrated skill development in preparing graduates for the digital economy. It shows that skill development is not only a pedagogical concern, but also a policy priority with implications for economic competitiveness, social mobility, and workforce equity. Recommendations: The findings underscore the importance of embedding authentic, workplace‑aligned learning opportunities across disciplines. Universities should prioritize the integration of English‑medium communication tasks, digital‑tool proficiency, and problem‑based learning within regular coursework. Policymakers should continue strengthening industry partnerships, investing in teacher training, and designing scalable micro‑credential pathways that address emerging skill demands. Employers may also benefit from closer collaboration with universities to co‑develop experiential learning opportunities and performance‑based assessments that mirror real-world expectations. Research Limitations: This study was limited by its reliance on a single institutional context, which may constrain generalizability. The use of self‑report measures introduces potential perceptual bias, and the cross‑sectional design restricts the ability to infer long‑term skill development trajectories or causal pathways. Perceptual measures of policy exposure and readiness may inflate observed relationships among variables. Future studies should incorporate multi-institutional samples, longitudinal tracking, and triangulated data sources, including employer evaluations and performance‑based assessments. Future Research: Future investigations may explore moderating variables such as program type, digital access, socioeconomic background, or prior work experience to understand variation in skill development outcomes. Comparative studies across ASEAN countries would also provide insight into differences in regional policy implementation. Additionally, mixed‑method approaches, combining surveys with interviews, classroom observations, or learning analytics, could offer deeper insights into how policy initiatives are enacted at the instructional level and how students experience skill development over time.

title: Examining the role of social media influencers in shaping perceptions of sustainable supply chain practices in Egypt
summary: Social media influencers have become central intermediaries in communicating corporate sustainability, yet it remains unclear how their characteristics shape stakeholder judgments about sustainable supply chains in emerging markets. To address this gap, the present study draws on the Elaboration Likelihood Model, informed by Stakeholder Theory, to examine how influencer credibility, engagement, perceived greenwashing risk, and economic constraints relate to trust, perceived supply chain transparency, and perceived adoption of sustainable practices in Egypt. Data were collected from 300 respondents, comprising both consumers and supply chain professionals, and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, multi-group analysis, and a bootstrapped mediation decomposition. The results show that credibility was positively associated with trust and transparency, whereas engagement functioned only as a weak peripheral cue; greenwashing risk, in turn, was negatively associated with trust. Although international influencers were rated as more trustworthy overall, local influencers were more strongly associated with trust and transparency when the message was context-specific, thereby revealing a credibility–context paradox. Economic constraints were related to perceived adoption through two opposing pathways: they were negatively associated with adoption directly but positively associated with it indirectly through trust and transparency; importantly, these relationships did not differ between consumers and professionals. Because the design is cross-sectional, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. Taken together, the study clarifies when and why influencer cues shape sustainability judgments and offers evidence-based guidance for influencer selection under economic pressure.

title: Pengaruh Komite Audit, Kepemilikan Institusional, dan Struktur Kepemilikan terhadap Kepatuhan Pelaporan Keuangan
summary: Timely and transparent financial reporting is essential for maintaining investor confidence, reducing information asymmetry, and supporting accountability in public companies. In the food and beverage manufacturing sub-sector, complex operations and post-pandemic reporting adjustments make compliance with financial reporting deadlines an important governance issue. This study aims to examine the effect of the audit committee, institutional ownership, and ownership structure on financial reporting compliance in food and beverage sub-sector manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022-2024 period. This research is grounded in agency theory and signaling theory, which explain how internal and external monitoring mechanisms shape management behavior in timely and transparent financial disclosure. This study aims to examine the effect of the audit committee, institutional ownership, and ownership structure on financial reporting compliance in food and beverage sub-sector manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022-2024 period. This research is grounded in agency theory and signaling theory, which explain how internal and external monitoring mechanisms shape management behavior in timely and transparent financial disclosure. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from annual reports and financial statements published on the official website of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (www.idx.co.id). The population consisted of 95 food and beverage manufacturing companies, and a census sampling technique was applied, resulting in 285 firm-year observations across three years of financial statements. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the Cochrane-Orcutt transformation to address autocorrelation problems. The results show that the audit committee has a positive and significant effect on financial reporting compliance, institutional ownership has a negative and significant effect, while ownership structure has no significant effect. The adjusted R-squared value of 0.552 indicates that the three independent variables explain 55.2% of the variation in financial reporting compliance. These findings imply that strengthening audit committee independence and competence and maintaining effective regulatory supervision are more decisive for improving reporting compliance than ownership concentration alone.

title: Green Finance and the Transformation of Agricultural Structure in China: Empirical Evidence from Urban Panel Data (2013–2023)
summary: Green finance (GF) offers sustainable solutions to challenges in agricultural sustainable development. This study examines the impact and mechanism of GF on the transformation of agricultural structure (AST). The problem statement highlights that although China emphasizes the establishment of a rural financial system and takes rural revitalization as a national strategy, issues related to innovative rural financial products and promoting rural economic development remain challenging. Using a dataset with 2505 observations spanning the period of 2013–2023 on China’s urban population, we utilize a two-way fixed effects model to explore the relationship between GF and AST. In addition, a mediation effect model is constructed to analyze the impact of GF on AST from the perspectives of green sustainable innovation (GSI), green consumption levels (GCL), and credit allocation efficiency (CAE). To account for regional disparities, we conducted heterogeneity analyses both at the urban level and by geographic region. The results indicate that GF effectively stimulates AST by optimizing CAE, enhancing GCL, and promoting GSI. Specifically, an increase in the share of agricultural inputs supporting sustainable and green development significantly altered the structure of agricultural outputs. Additionally, the findings suggest that the influence of GF on AST shows regional heterogeneity, which is more significant in low-urbanized cities in the eastern and central regions of China. This study provides insights into how global agriculture can seize opportunities for sustainable development within the context of the GF.

title: Pengaruh Literasi Keuangan dan Edukasi Pasar Modal terhadap Keputusan Berinvestasi di Galeri Investasi Syariah Studi pada Mahasiswa FEBI UIN STS Jambi
summary: The development of the digital economy has increased public awareness of the importance of investment as a means of achieving long-term financial goals. This study aims to analyze the influence of financial literacy and capital market education on students' investment decisions at the Sharia Investment Gallery of the Faculty of Islamic Economics and Business, Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin State Islamic University of Jambi. This research employed a quantitative method, with data collected through questionnaires and analyzed using statistical techniques. The results indicate that financial literacy and capital market education have a positive and significant effect on students' investment decisions, both partially and simultaneously. These findings suggest that higher levels of financial literacy and better understanding of the capital market lead to more effective investment decisions among students. Therefore, enhancing financial literacy and capital market education is essential to support sound investment decision-making among university students.

title: The Role Supply Chain Management Practices in Enhancing Competitive Advantage and Firm Performance in Handloom Textile Industry
summary: Abstract: Handloom textile firms experience several difficulties due to inefficiencies within their supply chains, limitations in technology adoption, and increased competition. In this regard, there is a need for efficient supply chain management to boost the organizational performance of such firms. This study seeks to determine the effect of supply chain management practices on firm performance via the mediating role of sustained competitive advantage in the handloom textile industry. The research adopted a quantitative design and data were collected through purposive sampling of respondents in handloom textile firms based in Karur, Tamil Nadu. The data analysis process involved the use of PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 and the results indicated that supplier relationship management, information sharing, inventory management, logistics effectiveness and technology integration have significant effects on sustained competitive advantage, which has a significant effect on firm performance. The structural model showed high predictive validity, where the independent variables accounted for 68.5% (R2 = 0.685) of the variance in Sustained Competitive Advantage, while Sustained Competitive Advantage explained 68.5% (R2 = 0.685) of the variance in Firm Performance. title: Corporate climate risk and public health disclosure: does digital transformation matter?
summary: Introduction Climate risk is playing an increasingly important role in shaping corporate behavior and non-financial disclosure. This study examines the nonlinear relationship between corporate climate risk (CR) and public health disclosure (PHD) using panel data from Chinese listed companies over the period 2000-2024. Methods Empirically, this study employs a two-way fixed effects model, a moderating effect model, and a quantile regression model, accompanied by formal cross-quantile tests to evaluate the non-linear dynamics, moderating channels, and heterogeneity across conditional PHD distributions. Results Four key findings emerge. First, CR exhibits a U-shaped relationship with PHD, and this relationship remains robust after a series of robustness and endogeneity checks. Second, conditional marginal effects and digital transformation (DT) specific turning points show that DT changes both the level and shape of the CR-PHD relationship, shifting the turning point to the right and attenuating the recovery of PHD at higher CR levels. Third, formal cross-quantile tests confirm that the CR and its quadratic term coefficients differ across the conditional PHD distribution. Fourth, the same tests identify significant differences across marketization and return on assets groups, whereas the differences across marginal profit groups are not statistically supported. Discussion These findings highlight the role of corporate CR and technological capabilities in shaping PHD. The U-shaped dynamic indicates that moderate CR initially depresses PHD, whereas severe risk forces strategic transparency to restore stakeholder trust and corporate reputation. Furthermore, the moderating effect of DT underscores that digital capabilities buffer firms against immediate risk pressures, altering their disclosure thresholds. The observed heterogeneity across marketization levels and financial performance emphasizes the need for differentiated regulatory oversight that accounts for regional institutional environments and corporate resource slack in driving sustainable corporate transparency.

title: Market uncertainty and supply chain endurance: Examining the complementary roles of marketing agility and organizational resilience
summary: This study develops and tests a dual-pathway model in which market uncertainty is substantially associated with agile marketing capability and organizational resilience—two theoretically distinct yet parallel capability domains. Supply chain endurance, defined as the capacity to maintain operational continuity and competitive positioning through proactive disruption avoidance rather than post-shock recovery alone, is the focal outcome and is explicitly differentiated from organizational resilience, which constitutes one of its enabling mechanisms. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the resource-based view, hypotheses are tested using PLS-SEM on survey data from 303 Indonesian manufacturing firms. Market uncertainty is substantially associated with both capabilities (agile marketing capability: β = 0.707, f 2 = 1.001; organizational resilience: β = 0.484, f 2 = 0.294), which subsequently strengthen supply chain endurance through partial mediation pathways (combined VAF = 47.4%). Discriminant validity is provisionally supported via Fornell-Larcker criteria and HTMT ratios (all six pairwise HTMT values below 0.85; Table 3b). Common method bias was assessed via Harman's single-factor test (dominant factor = 28.7%) and full collinearity VIF diagnostics (max VIF = 2.588), supporting negligible bias. Findings demonstrate that endurance emerges from balanced capability portfolios addressing uncertainty across demand-side and supply-side dimensions simultaneously, rather than from any singular operational competency. Theoretical contributions to dynamic capabilities theory, the resource-based view, and emerging market supply chain scholarship are discussed.

title: Pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility dan Enterprise Risk Management Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada Perusahaan Manufaktur yang Terdaftar di BEI Tahun 2021-2024
summary: Penelitian ini mengkaji pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) dan Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) terhadap nilai perusahaan manufaktur yang tercatat di Bursa Efek Indonesia sepanjang periode 2021–2024. Dengan pendekatan kuantitatif, penelitian ini mengolah data sekunder dari laporan tahunan dan laporan tahunan sebanyak 203 observasi. Pengungkapan CSR diukur melalui Corporate Social Responsibility Disclosure Index (CSRDI) berdasarkan GRI Standards 2021, sedangkan pengungkapan ERM diukur melalui Enterprise Risk Management Disclosure Index (ERMDI) yang mengacu pada COSO Framework . Nilai perusahaan diproksikan dengan rasio Price to Book Value (PBV), dan pengujian data dilakukan melalui regresi linier berganda dengan bantuan SPSS versi 27. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa CSR berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap nilai perusahaan semakin tinggi jarak CSR, semakin besar peningkatan nilai perusahaan yang terjadi. Sebaliknya, ERM berpengaruh negatif signifikan, yang mengindikasikan bahwa pengungkapan ERM belum menjadi pertimbangan utama investor dalam menilai perusahaan manufaktur. Temuan ini menegaskan relevansi Stakeholder Theory dalam menjelaskan peran CSR sebagai instrumen legitimasi sosial dan reputasi, sekaligus menunjukkan bahwa efektivitas ERM sangat bergantung pada kualitas implementasi dan persepsi pemangku kepentingan .

title: The Role Supply Chain Management Practices in Enhancing Competitive Advantage and Firm Performance in Handloom Textile Industry
summary: Abstract: Handloom textile firms experience several difficulties due to inefficiencies within their supply chains, limitations in technology adoption, and increased competition. In this regard, there is a need for efficient supply chain management to boost the organizational performance of such firms. This study seeks to determine the effect of supply chain management practices on firm performance via the mediating role of sustained competitive advantage in the handloom textile industry. The research adopted a quantitative design and data were collected through purposive sampling of respondents in handloom textile firms based in Karur, Tamil Nadu. The data analysis process involved the use of PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 and the results indicated that supplier relationship management, information sharing, inventory management, logistics effectiveness and technology integration have significant effects on sustained competitive advantage, which has a significant effect on firm performance. The structural model showed high predictive validity, where the independent variables accounted for 68.5% (R2 = 0.685) of the variance in Sustained Competitive Advantage, while Sustained Competitive Advantage explained 68.5% (R2 = 0.685) of the variance in Firm Performance. Keywords: Supply Chain Management, Handloom Textile Industry, Sustained Competitive Advantage, Firm Performance

title: Strategic Technology Adoption and Organizational Agility in the Digital Transformation Era
summary: Digital transformation has changed organizational management patterns and encouraged companies to improve their adaptability through the adoption of strategic technology. However, the success of digital transformation still faces challenges in integrating technology with organizational capabilities. This study aims to analyze the influence of strategic technology adoption on organizational agility in companies implementing digital technology in Surabaya, Indonesia. The study uses a quantitative approach with a survey method of 212 respondents consisting of managers and employees at digital technology-based companies in Surabaya. Data collection was carried out through a structured questionnaire, then analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS). The results of the study show that strategic technology adoption has a positive and significant effect on organizational agility through increasing business process flexibility, decision-making speed, and innovation capabilities. This research makes a theoretical contribution to the development of digital transformation management studies as well as practical implications for organizations in building adaptive and sustainable technology strategies.

title: Modern Slavery in Supply Chains: A Framing Perspective on Managerial Responses to Transparency Legislation
summary: ABSTRACT Innovative legislation aspires for an extra‐jurisdictional effect on modern slavery in supply chains through increased transparency. Evidence to date suggests that firms are not rising to this challenge, and, if anything, mandatory reporting practices are coalescing around superficial reports decoupled from policy objectives. To decide how the regulatory regime should best be adapted, it is important to understand not just the organizational‐level response but also the underlying managerial attitudes and behavior on which substantive practical action depends. The study utilized a photo elicitation method with 47 managers drawn from eight large UK construction firms. Framing theory was utilized to reveal four distinct managerial mindsets, each with different implications for policy and practice. These variants suggest that a one‐size‐fits‐all policy approach is suboptimal. Policy combining rewards and penalties, tailored to each framing group, is likely to be the most expedient in quickly improving managerial behavior. The existence of inconsistent framing within firms suggests that strategic policies are not being effectively embedded in managerial practice. In turn, this limits the impact that focal firms have in improving labor practices across multiple tiers of their supply chains. Reporting entities should not be treated as cohesive, unitary entities by stakeholders.

title: Blockchain-enabled anti-counterfeiting solutions in supply chains: a bibliometric and thematic analysis
summary: Blockchain technology has emerged as a critical application for supply chain anti-counterfeiting, offering decentralized and traceable solutions to enhance transparency and trust. This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 273 publications indexed in the Scopus database from 2017 to 2025 to clarify the core knowledge structure and developmental trends of the field. Using CiteSpace software, Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny to process the data, the study examines collaboration networks, keyword trends, timeline maps, citation bursts and co-citation patterns. The analysis investigates the prominent authors, institutions and countries contributing to the field, identifying seven major research clusters and evolutionary trends. The findings highlight the research hotspots and current state of blockchain technology in supply chain anti-counterfeiting, while identifying existing research challenges and future directions to facilitate widespread adoption.

title: The Influence of Sales Growth and Earnings Management on Financial Performance: The Role of Firm Size Moderation
summary: This study analyzes the influence of sales growth and earnings management on financial performance and examines whether firm size moderates the relationship in Consumer Non-Cyclicals companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the period 2021–2024. Financial performance is proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), earnings management by discretionary accruals using the Modified Jones Model, sales growth by annual sales change, and firm size by the natural logarithm of total assets. The study uses a causal quantitative design with panel data and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) using EViews 12. Purposive sampling in the early stages resulted in 46 companies with 184 company-year observations; after outlier screening, 167 observations were used in the model estimation. The selected model was the Random Effects Model. The results showed that sales growth had no significant effect on financial performance (p = 0.2101), while earnings management had a positive and significant effect (p = 0.0126). Firm size significantly moderated the influence of sales growth on financial performance in a negative direction (p = 0.0488), thus acting as a pure moderator that weakened the sales growth–ROA relationship. Firm size was not proven to moderate the relationship between earnings management and financial performance (p = 0.4127). These findings suggest that revenue increases alone are not enough to increase profitability if operating costs and asset use are not managed efficiently, while reported ROA remains sensitive to discretionary accruals.

title: Realization Of The Economic Potential Of The Region In The Context Of Digital Transformation Of The Economy
summary: For the historical regions of the Russian Federation, the digital transformation of the economy, which is changing the usual understanding of processes in all spheres of life, is an additional obstacle to integration into the public, economic, social, scientific and innovative space of Russia. The article examines the realization of the economic potential of the Luhansk People's Republic in the context of the digital transformation of the economy for the full integration of historical regions into the digital space of Russia. The concept of the process of realizing the economic potential of the region in the context of the digital transformation of the economy is formulated. It is proposed to activate the economic potential of the region by activating its types, namely: natural resource, industrial, innovative, labor (personnel) and scientific and technical. The obstacles to the integration of historical regions and the LPR in particular into the digital space of Russia are outlined. The main directions of ensuring transparency and openness of digital services in the Republic are highlighted, which are aimed at creating a favorable investment climate, which will become the basis for realizing its economic potential.

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Supply Chain Management: A Systematic Analysis of Technologies, Applications and Performance
summary: The growing complexity of supply chains has made it more important than ever to use smart technologis that can make operations better help with choices and make responses faster. Artificial Intelligence or AI has become a technology that is changing the way supply chains work. It uses data to look at things predict what might happen and automate tasks. This study looks at how Artificial Intelligence's used in Supply Chain Management and how it helps important parts of the supply chain. The study reviews the research that already exists on AI technologies like machine learning, predictive analytics, smart automation and big data analytics. It looks at how these technologies used in things like predicting what customers will want managing inventory making logistics better handling warehouses working with suppliers and managing risks in the supply chain. A detailed look at the research is done to find the areas where AI is used the benefits it brings the problems it faces and what new research is happening. The results show that AI can make predicting customer demand manage inventory more efficiently improve how goods are moved help people make decisions faster and make the whole supply chain stronger. There are still problems like the cost of using AI, the quality of the data, security issues combining AI with old systems and needing people who know how to use AI. The study also finds where more research is needed and creates a model that connects AI abilities with how well the supply chain works. The results give a starting point for studies, about using AI to change supply chains and build smarter, quicker and more efficient systems.

title: Fintech Partnerships and Perceived Financial Performance of Commercial Banks Listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange in Kenya
summary: The relationship between fintech partnerships and financial performance has attracted increasing attention as commercial banks increasingly rely on external technology providers to enhance digital capabilities, develop innovative financial products, and improve operational efficiency.This study examined the association between fintech partnerships and perceived financial performance among commercial banks listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) in Kenya, drawing on transaction cost economics (TCE) and a positivist research philosophy.Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires administered to managers responsible for digital transformation, information technology, strategy, and operations across all 11 NSE-listed commercial banks.Of the 110 questionnaires distributed, 84 valid responses were obtained, representing a response rate of 76.4%.The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation analysis, and simple linear regression.A strong and statistically significant positive association was identified between fintech partnerships and perceived financial performance (r = 0.820, p < 0.01).The regression analysis further indicated that fintech partnerships significantly predicted perceived financial performance (R² = 0.672, p < 0.001).These findings suggest that stronger collaboration between commercial banks and fintech firms is associated with improved perceptions of financial performance.In particular, partnerships involving digital payment systems, application programming interfaces (APIs), and joint product development may provide avenues for strengthening banks' digital capabilities and competitive positioning.However, the effectiveness of such partnerships is likely to depend on appropriate governance structures, risk-management mechanisms, data-security arrangements, and regulatory compliance.The findings provide empirical support for fintech partnerships as a potentially important strategic mechanism through which listed commercial banks in Kenya can respond to technological change while enhancing their perceived financial performance.

title: Crisis to resilience: tracing direct, indirect and induced tourism impacts in Kenya’s economy
summary: Tourism shocks can propagate well beyond visitor-facing industries through production networks, factor incomes, and household consumption. This study estimates the economy-wide effects of the COVID-19 tourism shock in Kenya using the Kenya Tourism Satellite Account (TSA) 2019 and publicly available Kenya Social Accounting Matrices (SAMs). Separate product-level final-demand shocks are constructed for inbound and domestic tourism in 2020 and 2021 relative to the 2019 benchmark. The combined visitor-demand contraction is estimated at KSh338.8 billion in 2020 and KSh174.2 billion in 2021. Using the 2019 Kenya SAM, these shocks generate estimated economy-wide gross-output contractions of KSh770.8 billion and KSh408.8 billion, respectively, alongside factor-value-added effects of KSh396.1 billion and KSh206.8 billion. Direct tourism employment-equivalent contractions are estimated at approximately 508,000 positions in 2020 and 249,000 in 2021. Inbound tourism accounts for most of the persistent 2021 shortfall, while domestic tourism recovers substantially faster. Transportation, accommodation, and food services experience the largest effects, with sizeable spillovers into trade, processed foods, agriculture, and business services. Structural sensitivity analysis using the 2021 Kenya SAM yields approximately 10% lower gross-output effects while preserving the direction and principal sectoral ranking of the findings. The results demonstrate both Kenya’s vulnerability to external tourism-demand shocks and the value of domestic tourism resilience, supporting policies that strengthen domestic and regional markets, supply-chain resilience, economic diversification, and inclusive crisis-response mechanisms.

title: Fintech, Digital Banking, and Profitability Under Macroeconomic Pressure: Evaluating Regulatory and Institutional Implications for Indonesia’s Banking System
summary: The digital banking era has introduced risks and opportunities that significantly affect bank profitability. This study examines 28 banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) between 2020 and 2022, focusing on the influence of credit risk, digital banking, and fintech on profitability, measured in this study by Return on Assets (ROA). Employing panel data analysis through EViews 12, two regression models were tested, one excluding and one including GDP as a control variable. Comparative results underscore Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) as the most consistent determinant, exerting a significant negative effect on ROA. While peerto-peer (P2P) lending initially appeared to hinder profitability, its impact diminished once macroeconomic conditions were controlled for. Moreover, although mobile banking adoption continues to expand, its immediate contribution to profitability remains statistically insignificant within this sample. Overall, the findings highlight credit risk as the primary concern, suggesting that stronger regulatory frameworks and enhanced collaboration between banks and fintech firms are essential to safeguarding financial stability. These insights emphasise the need for policymakers and banking executives to prioritise credit risk management while fostering a cooperative ecosystem to navigate the complexities of the digital transformation.

title: Signaling ESG disclosure readiness before listing: text-mining evidence from Indian IPO prospectuses
summary: Introduction Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure has become central to how firms establish credibility with capital markets, yet its role at the point of market entry remains underexamined. This study investigates how Indian firms communicate ESG readiness in mainboard initial public offering (IPO) prospectuses, measuring the intensity and thematic composition of ESG-related language rather than treating disclosure as a proxy for ESG performance or quality. Methods The analytical sample comprises 310 non-financial operating-company IPO prospectuses issued from FY2021-22 to FY2025-26. Prospectus text was cleaned, segmented into sentences, and embedded using Sentence-BERT. Each sentence was matched by cosine similarity to reference sentences derived from a Baier et al.-based ESG taxonomy comprising three pillars, ten categories, and forty subcategories; sentences scoring 0.45 or above were classified as ESG-related and assigned to the corresponding pillar and subcategory. In addition to the textual analysis, the study also carried out firm-level regressions relating pillar-specific disclosure to issuer characteristics and board structure, controlling for sector, year and document length. Results ESG-related sentences constitute, on average, 11.382% of total sentences across the sample. Governance disclosure is significantly more prevalent (8.605% of clean sentences) than social (1.462%) or environmental (1.314%) disclosure, with governance accounting for 75.5% of all ESG-classified sentences. Disclosure intensity and thematic emphasis vary meaningfully across financial years, industry sectors, and ESG subcategories. Supplementary regressions reveal pillar-specific rather than uniform associations between issuer characteristics and ESG disclosure, while board size and board independence are jointly associated with governance disclosure in a parsimonious specification. Discussion These findings are consistent with, but do not establish, a credibility-related signaling channel centered on governance disclosure. In the IPO prospectuses governance-related content dominates ESG communication at listing, while environmental and social disclosure remain comparatively limited and unevenly distributed across sectors and time.

title: The Visible Hand, the Invisible Hand, and the Firm's Own Hand What Propels ESG Engagement in Chinese Companies
summary: ABSTRACT This paper surveys the empirical literature on the antecedents of corporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) engagement in China, distinguishing substantive ESG actions, ESG disclosure, externally assigned ESG performance, and symbolic or reputational responses. Synthesizing 126 studies published between 2004 and 2024 in leading journals on the UTD, FT and ABS lists, we develop a tripartite analytical model in which forces at the government, market and firm levels jointly determine ESG behavior through three interaction logics, namely mutual reinforcement, substitution and contingency. The evidence identifies regulatory pressure, policy incentives, state ownership and political connections, together with media scrutiny, product market competition, institutional investors and customer demands, as well as organizational resources, governance arrangements and strategic orientation, as the principal antecedents of ESG engagement. Their relative importance varies systematically over time and across regions, industries, and ownership types, although changes in research attention do not by themselves establish a transition in Chinese ESG governance. We further document considerable theoretical fragmentation, as institutional, stakeholder, and resource‐based perspectives are widely applied but seldom combined. The survey concludes with an agenda for future research covering meta‐analytic validation, firm‐level mechanisms, heterogeneity across ESG dimensions, digitalization and cross‐country comparison.

title: Evaluating large language models for complex supply chain optimisation: a focus on routing problems
summary: This study evaluates the ability of general-purpose large language models (LLMs) to solve structured logistics and supply chain optimisation problems. We benchmark nine routing and procurement-routing problems, ranging from the travelling salesman problem and vehicle routing problem to richer variants with capacity limits and time windows, among others. We also introduce an additional inventory-routing extension. Using fixed instances, prompt templates, and external verification scripts, we evaluate eight GenAI model snapshots across three benchmark rounds, from early 2025 models to newer 2026 releases. Outputs are checked for feasibility, objective-value correctness, and solution quality relative to solver-based references or dedicated heuristic incumbents. The results show that LLMs can often generate feasible and high-quality solutions for unconstrained or moderately constrained routing problems, but their reliability decreases as operational constraints interact. Newer models improve feasibility and arithmetic consistency, especially on the core routing families, yet highly constrained procurement-routing and inventory-routing instances remain difficult. Comparisons with problem-tailored heuristics show that advanced GenAI can sometimes produce competitive candidate solutions, but dedicated heuristics remain more robust and computationally efficient. Overall, the study positions GenAI as a promising lightweight decision-support companion for logistics optimisation, while emphasising the continued need for external verification, structured prompting, and problem-specific optimisation methods.

title: PRODUCTION, TRANSACTION, AND LOGISTICS COSTS IN ALGERIAN AGRIBUSINESS: A LITERATUREREVIEW OF ECONOMETRIC AND SUPPLY CHAIN EVIDENCE
summary: This article investigates why Algeria’s agri-food import bill remains close to USD 10 billion annually despite increasing domestic agricultural production. It examines this apparent mismatch from the perspective of cost integration and the resilience of the agri-food sector during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The study employs an integrative literature review combining evidence from published ARDL, NARDL and VAR studies with a PRISMA-guided review of recent research on agri-food supply chains and sectoral evidence from Saharan cereal and poultry production. No new econometric models are estimated. The analysis focuses on four categories of costs related to fiscal policy, agricultural finance, structural transformation, and logistics and post-harvest losses. Evidence from previous ARDL studies is consistent with a Dutch-disease interpretation, although it does not confirm it. Existing VAR results indicate no statistically significant Granger-causal relationship between agricultural credit and output, while NARDL findings suggest that increases in decoupled subsidies may be associated with slower structural transformation. The review also identifies deficiencies in cold storage, traceability and supply-chain coordination as important sources of logistics and post-harvest costs. An illustrative calculation based on a 20% loss rate and an agricultural production value of approximately USD 35 billion suggests potential annual losses of around USD 7 billion; this figure should be interpreted as a scenario-based extrapolation rather than a national estimate. Overall, the findings suggest that Algeria’s resilience challenge stems not only from resource constraints but also from insufficient coordination between production, finance and logistics. The study highlights the need to redirect part of recurrent subsidies toward productive investment, combine agricultural credit with technical support and monitoring, and develop cold-chain infrastructure alongside digital inventory and traceability systems.

title: The phenomenon of earnings management : the case of financially distressed small and medium-sized enterprises in the European Union
summary: Η παρούσα διατριβή εξετάζει τη σχέση μεταξύ της οικονομικής δυσχέρειας των επιχειρήσεων της Ευρωζώνης και της υιοθέτησης λογιστικών πολιτικών που αποσκοπούν στη χειραγώγηση των χρηματοοικονομικών τους αποτελεσμάτων (earnings management). Για τον έλεγχο των ερευνητικών υποθέσεων χρησιμοποιείται ένα εκτενές δείγμα μη εισηγμένων επιχειρήσεων από 17 χώρες της Ευρωζώνης, καλύπτοντας την πενταετία 2012–2016. Η εστίαση στις μη εισηγμένες οντότητες υπαγορεύεται από τη σχετική βιβλιογραφική υποεκπροσώπησή τους, ιδίως υπό καθεστώς χρηματοοικονομικής στενότητας (Dutzi and Rausch 2016; Saleh and Ahmed 2005). Η αξιολόγηση της οικονομικής δυσχέρειας πραγματοποιήθηκε μέσω του υποδείγματος Z-score του Altman. Προς ενίσχυση της αξιοπιστίας των εκτιμήσεων, το δείγμα εμπλουτίστηκε με επιχειρήσεις που πτώχευσαν κατά την εξεταζόμενη περίοδο, επιτρέποντας τη χαρτογράφηση της λογιστικής συμπεριφοράς στο τελικό στάδιο της αφερεγγυότητας. Η διαχείριση των κερδών προσεγγίζεται διττά: μέσω των δεδουλευμένων λογιστικών μεγεθών (accruals earnings management) με βάση το υπόδειγμα του Kothari (2005), και μέσω της χειραγώγησης των πραγματικών δραστηριοτήτων (real earnings management) με τη χρήση των υποδειγμάτων της Roychowdhury (2006). Για την αντιμετώπιση του προβλήματος της ενδογένειας και τη διασφάλιση της δειγματικής εγκυρότητας, η στατιστική ανάλυση και ο έλεγχος των υποθέσεων διενεργήθηκαν με τη Μέθοδο των Γενικευμένων Ροπών (Generalized Method of Moments – GMM). Αποσκοπώντας στην περαιτέρω διερεύνηση της σχέσης οικονομικής δυσχέρειας και διαχείρισης κερδών, πραγματοποιήθηκαν τέσσερις επιμέρους μελέτες. Η πρώτη έδειξε ότι οι ευρωπαϊκές εμπορικές τράπεζες, όταν λειτουργούν υπό συνθήκες χρηματοοικονομικής πίεσης, παρουσιάζουν υποβαθμισμένη ποιότητα κερδών, με σημαντικές επιπτώσεις για τη χρηματοδότηση των ΜΜΕ. Η δεύτερη ανέδειξε ότι οι ελληνικές ΠΑΕ με αυξημένες αγωνιστικές επιτυχίες εμφανίζουν υψηλότερα επίπεδα χειραγώγησης λογιστικών αποτελεσμάτων, κυρίως λόγω των απαιτήσεων συμμόρφωσης με το Financial Fair Play. Η τρίτη κατέδειξε ότι οι ελληνικές ΜΜΕ που αντιμετωπίζουν χρηματοοικονομική στενότητα και αυξημένες φορολογικές υποχρεώσεις καταφεύγουν συχνότερα σε πρακτικές διαχείρισης κερδών για την ενίσχυση της ρευστότητας και της πιστοληπτικής τους εικόνας. Τέλος, η τέταρτη μελέτη επιβεβαίωσε ότι ισχυροί μηχανισμοί εταιρικής διακυβέρνησης περιορίζουν την υιοθέτηση ευκαιριακών λογιστικών πρακτικών. Συνολικά, τα εμπειρικά ευρήματα καταδεικνύουν ότι η οικονομική δυσχέρεια ενισχύει τη διαχείριση κερδών, ανεξαρτήτως χώρας ή κλάδου δραστηριοποίησης. Οι επιχειρήσεις φαίνεται να προτιμούν τη χειραγώγηση μέσω δεδουλευμένων λόγω του χαμηλότερου κόστους εφαρμογής της, ενώ τα φορολογικά κίνητρα και η ανάγκη πρόσβασης σε τραπεζική χρηματοδότηση αποτελούν βασικούς παράγοντες υποκίνησης. Αντίθετα, η αποτελεσματική εταιρική διακυβέρνηση αναδεικνύεται ως κρίσιμος μηχανισμός ελέγχου και περιορισμού των πρακτικών διαχείρισης κερδών.

title: The Impact of Tax Authority Coordination on the Financial Reporting Quality of Export Businesses in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the impact of tax authority coordination on the financial reporting quality of export businesses in Nigeria. The study adopted a quantitative research approach using a survey research design. Data were collected from 385 respondents comprising accountants, finance officers, and tax managers of export businesses registered with the Nigeria Export Promotion Council in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt. The study examined compliance certificate and Nigeria Revenue Service notification as dimensions of tax authority coordination, while earnings smoothing and earnings timeliness were used as measures of financial reporting quality. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis. The findings revealed that compliance certificate had a significant positive effect on earnings timeliness and a significant negative effect on earnings smoothing. Similarly, NRS notification had a significant positive effect on earnings timeliness and a significant negative effect on earnings smoothing. The study concludes that stronger tax authority coordination significantly improves financial reporting quality among export businesses in Nigeria by promoting accountability, transparency, accurate record-keeping, and timely reporting. It recommends strengthening the compliance certificate system, improving Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) notification and communication channels, enhancing monitoring of financial reporting practices, and promoting timely exchange of financial and tax information between export businesses and relevant government agencies.

title: Leadership and the integration challenge: A grounded theory study of digital transformation in AECO
summary: This study examines how leaders in a large and complex public organization within the Architecture, Engineering, Construction and Operations (AECO) sector perceive the conditions for digitally oriented leadership. Using a grounded theory approach, twenty in-depth interviews with managers and project managers were analyzed through open and focused coding. The analysis identified Lack of integration of digital work systems as the core category summarizing the main barriers to digital transformation. Four interrelated categories - Lack of vision and purpose, Limited usability, Silo organization, and Organizational inertia -were found to constrain leaders’ ability to adopt digitally oriented leadership practices. The study contributes a grounded theoretical explanation showing how barriers operating at different leadership levels collectively reinforce the lack of integration of digital work systems, thereby constraining digitally oriented leadership and digital transformation. The study indicates that digital transformation cannot be achieved through technology alone but requires organizational and leadership integration supported by clear strategies, cross-functional collaboration, and adequate digital competence. These findings advance understanding of leadership conditions in digital transformation and offer practical implications for enhancing leadership capacity in AECO organizations.

title: Digital Transformation of Procurement: A Case Study of E-Procurement System Implementation
summary: Background: Indirect procurement in precision manufacturing remains under-digitised, generating high transaction volumes, limited spend visibility, and weak compliance enforcement. This study examines the selection and implementation of an e-Procurement platform for the indirect purchasing function of a high-precision optical components manufacturer. Methods: A qualitative action-research methodology, combining a narrative literature review, a weighted multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) across 16 candidate platforms, and participatory implementation across four data preparation workstreams. Results: The selected platform outperformed the competing finalist with a raw evaluation score of 82 vs. 81 (out of 90 scored criteria; 120 if the zero-weighted Sourcing criterion is included) and a weighted score of 23.3 vs. 22.9, with System Quality the decisive differentiator. Implementation outcomes include an 85.7% reduction in payment term codes (133 to 19), a 68.75% reduction in unit of measure codes (48 to 15), restructuring a 22-category taxonomy into 10-group and 56-subcategory, and a projected 75% reduction in purchase order lead time (a process-mapping estimate, pending post-go-live validation). 105 users were trained across six role categories before go-live. Conclusions: Data governance is a strategic prerequisite. The framework offers a replicable approach for precision manufacturing, with ERP integration, multi-level approval workflow design, and role-differentiated training as success factors.

title: Circumscribed disruption: FinTech narratives in central banking
summary: The proliferation of financial technologies has sparked debate about their capacity to disrupt the political, regulatory, and monetary status quo. In policy discourse, FinTech is often framed as a balance between supporting innovation and safeguarding financial stability. This article examines how central bankers and monetary authority officials construct this balance in public speeches. Using 789 FinTech-related speeches from the Bank for International Settlements archive, I qualitatively identify recurring thematic frames and classify sentences across the corpus using zero-shot classification with a DeBERTa-based model. The analysis finds convergence around a shared policy narrative of circumscribed disruption. FinTech is welcomed as a source of innovation, inclusion, competition, and growth, provided its effects remain compatible with existing frameworks of financial stability and regulatory oversight. Within this shared narrative, however, there is bounded divergence around politically exposed frames. Descriptive country-level models show that lower-income contexts more strongly emphasise inclusion and growth, while higher-income contexts emphasise innovation. The article contributes to central bank communication research by showing how monetary authorities narrate a complex, partly politicised issue in ways consistent with an epistemic community lens. Methodologically, it combines qualitative frame construction, zero-shot classification, and manual validation to study narrative variation at scale.

title: Digital transformation in local government: a hybrid bibliometric and systematic literature review
summary: Purpose This study aims to explore the intellectual context of research on digital transformation in local governments to integrate fragmented streams of research into a coherent body of knowledge. To this end, it analyzes the growth, conceptual development, research hotspots, knowledge base, research methods and future research directions. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric–systematic literature review was conducted. The bibliometric analysis involved 915 English-language, open-access journal articles indexed in Scopus that were published between 2010 and 2025, using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. Thematic synthesis was conducted using 294 full-text studies following the PRISMA2020 guidelines to identify major themes, theories, methods, findings and research gaps. Findings Recent years have seen this work progress from e-government and administrative digitization to an overarching smart governance and organizational transformation, touching upon public value, citizen participation, digital divide and big data. This review reveals that technological capabilities are not sufficient for digital transformation; leadership skills, institutional capacities, collaborative governance and organizational readiness are also important. Issues of digital divide, cybersecurity, ethical governance and implications of emerging technologies, especially artificial intelligence, remain. Originality/value This study takes a step forward in the review process by combining bibliometric mapping and thematic synthesis, bringing disconnected information together as a coherent representation of digital transformation from the perspective of governance and offering evidence-based insights into the priorities of future research, policy and digitally-enabled local government change.

title: GREEN HRM DAN GREEN OCB DALAM MENDORONG KINERJA LINGKUNGAN MELALUI GREEN INNOVATION
summary: This study aims to examine the mediating role of Green Innovation in the relationship between Green Human Resource Management (Green HRM), Green Organizational Citizenship Behavior (Green OCB), and Environmental Performance in local government agencies in Lebak Regency, Indonesia. This study employs a quantitative approach using a survey method involving 121 respondents. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that Green HRM has a positive and significant effect on both Green Innovation and Environmental Performance. Green OCB has a positive effect on Environmental Performance, but does not have a significant effect on Green Innovation. Although Green Innovation has a positive effect on Environmental Performance, it does not mediate the relationship between Green HRM and Environmental Performance, nor the relationship between Green OCB and Environmental Performance. This study contributes to the development of the green management literature by providing empirical evidence from the public sector and recommends strengthening Green HRM practices, fostering an environmentally oriented organizational culture, and enhancing sustainable innovation to improve environmental performance in the public sector.

title: Corporate Governance, Financial Policy, and Corporate Investment Efficiency: Rethinking the Role of Family Ownership in Emerging Market
summary: Purpose: This study aims to determine the effect of corporate governance mechanisms and financial policy on the efficiency of corporate investment and to examine the moderating role of family ownership in the emerging market. Design/Methodology/Approach: Using panel regression techniques, the study tests the proposed relationships using balanced panel data from non-financial companies listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) for 2015 to 2022. Findings: The study shows that board independence, CEO duality, CEO qualifications enhance investment efficiency, while board gender diversity has a negative relationship with investment efficiency. Likewise, financial leverage reduces investment efficiency, while dividend policy improves it. Family ownership is an important boundary condition: it strengthens the positive relationship between CEO duality, CEO qualifications, and Corporate investment efficiency, and the negative relationship between financial leverage and investment efficiency. Practical implications: These insights will help regulators develop family business governance codes, remind boards of the advantages of CEO duality and qualifications for capital allocation, advise family businesses against over-leverage, and demonstrate an efficient way to invest by focusing on dividend policy. Originality/Value: It is the first study to consider governance mechanisms, financial policy and family ownership in the same study to provide a more synthesized answer to what is constraining and driving investment efficiency in emerging markets. It provides novel insights into the interconnection between financial policy and investment results that are influenced by family control.

title: Unlocking the influencing factors of innovation information disclosure: a multi-level analysis
summary: This study investigates the multilevel influencing factors of innovation information disclosure by adopting a multidimensional index and uses fixed-effects regression models among all firms listed in China’s A-share market from 2013 to 2022. Existing studies with a primary emphasis at the firm level largely overlook industry and macroeconomic factors. This study systematically investigates how multilevel factors affect innovation information disclosure, particularly in the context of balancing the trade-off between innovation protection and information transparency. This study suggests that the quality of accounting information disclosure and enterprise digital transformation at the firm level; the presence of high-tech, manufacturing, and technology-intensive enterprises at the industry level; and the digital economy, Broadband China and industrial structure rationalization at the macro level positively affect innovation information disclosure. We also examine the inverted U-shaped relationship between R&D intensity at the firm level and innovation information disclosure. The results remain robust after a series of robustness checks. Furthermore, we explore whether the synergistic effects between the influencing factors at the firm and industry levels, firm and macro levels, and industry and macro levels have a negative effect on innovation information disclosure. The implications of this study are significant for improving corporate innovation capabilities and future growth potential. These findings provide insights for policymakers to design supportive environments, help industry practitioners in strategic disclosure decisions, provide a multilevel framework for researchers and guide investors to make more informed investments. Ultimately, these contributions serve the long-term goal of fostering a more transparent and dynamic national innovation ecosystem, which drives sustainable economic growth and technological advancement.

title: Quality of earnings and carbon emission disclosure: Insights from a meta-analysis approach
summary: The relationship between the quality of earnings, as measured by real earnings management, and carbon emission disclosure has been a subject of central and controversial debate in studies on the transition towards a low-carbon economy. However, previous empirical studies have reached mixed conclusions. This study systematically and quantitatively examines the relationship between earnings quality and carbon-emission disclosure using a meta-analytical technique. By synthesizing prior research, our goal is to quantify how corporate carbon disclosures correlate with earnings quality while identifying key factors that influence this relationship, such as industry type, governance structures, and regulatory environments. The study reveals a moderate positive association between earnings quality and carbon-emission disclosure, demonstrating that companies with more transparent earnings practices provide detailed environmental information. Additionally, the results highlight the significant role of corporate governance and regulatory frameworks in shaping these dynamics. This research contributes to the ongoing conversation about sustainability reporting, underscoring the importance of financial integrity in fostering environmental accountability. This research builds upon existing knowledge by compiling previous findings on the precision of corporate earnings and carbon emissions disclosure. In conclusion, the study calls for stronger regulatory measures and corporate governance to improve the reliability and comparability of carbon disclosure practices.

title: Green Leadership and Sustainable Business Performance in MSMEs: The Mediating Role of Green Innovation and the Moderating Role of Organizational Culture
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of Green Leadership on Sustainable Business Performance in micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), with Green Innovation serving as a mediating mechanism and Organizational Culture as a moderating variable. The study adopts a quantitative explanatory research design involving 100 respondents consisting of MSME owners/managers and employees. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with the assistance of SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that Green Leadership has a positive and significant effect on Green Innovation (β = 0.656; p < 0.001) and Sustainable Business Performance (β = 0.487; p < 0.001). Green Innovation also has a positive and significant effect on Sustainable Business Performance (β = 0.276; p = 0.004). Meanwhile, Green Leadership does not have a significant effect on Organizational Culture (β = 0.166; p = 0.118), and Organizational Culture does not significantly affect Sustainable Business Performance (β = −0.085; p = 0.308). Organizational Culture has a positive and significant direct effect on Green Innovation (β = 0.147; p = 0.048), but does not moderate either the Green Leadership–Green Innovation relationship or the Green Innovation–Sustainable Business Performance relationship. These findings highlight the importance of Green Leadership and Green Innovation in enhancing sustainable business performance among MSMEs.
